page: Microsoft Azure E2as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at an indicated frequency of 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates a single physical core exposed as two dedicated vCPUs via multi-threading, paired with 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio characteristic of memory-oriented enterprise cloud profiles.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage, operating disklessly by default and requiring external block storage such as Azure Premium Storage. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs included. Benchmark measurements reveal solid single-threaded performance, with stress-ng single-core execution reaching the top 25% tier and Geekbench single-core scoring 1,453 points. However, total multi-threaded scaling remains constrained by the dual-vCPU ceiling, as reflected in low multi-core Geekbench results (1,762 points) and moderate PassMark CPU scores.

Synthetic memory bandwidth tests record 128.6 GB/sec for small cached reads and 30.8 GB/sec for uncached reads, supporting average tier memory throughput in PassMark testing. With its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the E2as_v5 delivers cost-efficient memory density without requiring excessive compute allocation. It is functionally suited for small-footprint in-memory caches, lightweight relational database workloads, staging environments, and memory-intensive microservices that require substantial memory capacity relative to low concurrent compute demands.
description: Microsoft Azure E2as_v5 is a memory-optimized cloud instance provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V, running on an AMD EPYC 7763 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz. The configuration delivers 2 vCPUs across a single physical core, coupled with 16.0 GB of system memory for an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, plus a 32 MB L3 cache. It includes no bundled local storage, relying on attached network storage such as Azure Premium Storage, and omits hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate capable single-core execution alongside modest multi-core capacity strictly bound by its two-thread limit. Memory subsystem performance is steady, achieving 30.8 GB/sec in uncached block reads. This resource profile provides cost-effective memory density for small in-memory caches, lightweight databases, and memory-heavy microservices.
